title: Build a Jev agent worker router
description: Route one agent task to research, writing or review with a typed Jev choice, a durable handoff and an explicit failure path. Test the whole workflow before scaling it.

source.title: Jev in the Agent Loop: A Complete Guide to Decision-Layer Automation

guide_authors.name: Appit Studio
guide_authors.role: Editorial guide; AI-assisted drafting and technical verification

connections.step: Rebuild the available action menu from the latest observation and verify the outcome after a selected action
connections.why: NO1ennn links Browser Use's Jev Ultrafast repository. Its bounded operation and target choices illustrate why a dispatcher must refresh eligible choices after state changes, although it dispatches browser actions rather than research and writing workers.
connections.limitations: MIT experimental Python browser agent, not a worker queue or permission authority. Live browser work needs Chrome, TypeSafe and a separate text-model credential for typing; observed page state can leave the host and provider usage may be billed. This guide did not execute its live loop.

connections.step: Route among a host-owned closed set of currently eligible capabilities and record the execution result
connections.why: jev-layer provides an optional Node/MCP route-and-receipt pattern for an existing harness. It is a separate route for readers who already have capability discovery and execution; NO1ennn does not name it, and it does not implement the article's Python file queues.
connections.limitations: Independent MIT Node.js 20+ package, not a Python dispatcher or executor. Its demo provider is offline and deterministic; TypeSafe or OpenRouter modes send bounded state to a remote provider and may incur charges. Its fail-open result hands control back to host policy, which must still enforce approvals and permissions.

faqs.question: How do I route an agent task to the next worker with Jev?
faqs.answer: Build a current list of eligible workers, send the goal and completed evidence with a Choice question, and validate the returned key in code. Save one durable handoff; send unclear, invalid or failed decisions to review.

faqs.question: Does a high Jev confidence mean the chosen worker is correct?
faqs.answer: No. Choice confidence describes the concentration of its answer distribution, not a guarantee that the route is correct. Treat 0.85 as a starting example, then tune a review threshold on labeled cases and check untouched cases separately.

faqs.question: What happens if the TypeSafe request times out?
faqs.answer: Record the error and keep the task in a durable review or existing fallback queue. Catch connection and timeout failures as well as API errors; do not treat a missing model answer as approval to run a worker.

faqs.question: Is Jev Ultrafast a worker router?
faqs.answer: No. The source-mentioned Browser Use project routes among freshly observed browser operations and targets. It teaches the changing-menu pattern, while your application must still define workers, queues, permissions and completion checks.
